extracted.intended_audience: poets, literary critics, and the educated reading public
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and evaluative principles for writing and judging poetry and literary criticism, focusing on style, prosody, the critic's temper, and how sound should reflect sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abhorrence of Envy and Detraction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing which more denotes a great Mind, than the Abhorrence of Envy and Detraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A great mind avoids depreciating others; envy and detraction are common among unsuccessful poets and diminish moral stature. Praising contemporaries magnifies each writer's reputation; attacking peers (ignorance of the moderns, scribblers) is an inferior route to fame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candour and Ingenuity in Criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: How much more noble is the Fame that is built on Candour and Ingenuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and authors should be frank and ingenious in judgment — correct errors without rancour. Example: Addison's frank note to Pope about a mistake is praised as candour; criticism that helps improve is preferable to disparagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression and Application over Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit and fine Writing doth not consist so much in advancing Things that are new, as in giving Things that are known an agreeable Turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Living in later ages, writers rarely invent wholly new precepts; excellence lies in expressing and applying known truths with elegance and novelty of turn (Boileau's point). Horace's reputation rests largely on his way of expressing and applying precepts rather than inventing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Dogmatic, Imagineless Criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: There is nothing in the World so tiresome as the Works of those Criticks who write in a positive Dogmatick Way, without either Language, Genius, or Imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: issuing rigid rules or pronouncements devoid of language, genius, or imagination. Such dogmatic critics bore readers; good criticism requires taste, imaginative exemplification, and stylistic ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity, Elegance, and Perspicuity in Critical Observations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Observations ... are explained with that Elegance and Perspicuity in which they are delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical points should be set forth clearly and attractively and illustrated with apt allusions. Even common or received precepts gain force when presented with elegance and well-chosen examples (as in Horace and Boileau).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound must Echo Sense (match prosody to meaning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tis not enough no Harshness gives Offence, The Sound must seem an Eccho to the Sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poetic sound and rhythm should reflect the content: soft, flowing sounds for gentle images ('Soft is the Strain when Zephyr gently blows'), and rough, hoarse measures for violent action ('when loud Surges lash the sounding Shore, The hoarse rough Verse should like the Torrent roar'). The auditory quality should reinforce semantic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metrical variation to represent motion and action
rubrics_metrics.description: This double Motion of the Stone is admirably described in the Numbers of these Verses; As in the four first it is heaved up by several Spondees intermixed with proper Breathing places, and at last trundles down in a continual Line of Dactyls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ specific metrical devices (spondees, dactyls, breathing places) in ordered sequence to mimic physical or narrative motion (rise then fall), thereby aligning meter with imagery and movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid insipid smoothness and needless alexandrines
rubrics_metrics.description: The insipid Smoothness which some Readers are so much in Love with ... These Equal Syllables alone require ... ten low Words oft creep in one dull Line. A needless Alexandrine ends the Song, That like a wounded Snake, drags its slow Length along.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware monotonous equal-syllable lines, padding with expletives ('do'), or inserting unnecessary alexandrines that slow the verse. Variety and judicious rhythm are required to prevent dulness; the ear tires of unvaried smoothness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrate precepts by exemplary passages (criticism by exemplification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our English Author has after the same manner exemplified several of his Precepts in the very Precepts themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good critics demonstrate rules within their critical writing: use quoted passages to show the rule in practice. Exemplification strengthens persuasion and shows the critic's command of the art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual celebration among great contemporaries enhances reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest Wits ... celebrated one another with so much Generosity, that each of them receives an additional Lustre from his Contemporaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Friendly, generous mutual praise among high-calibre writers contributes to each author's fame; a literary climate of mutual esteem elevates reputations more than solitary brilliance accompanied by detraction.
